cmu_06-262.title: 06-262 Math Methods in Chemical Engineering
cmu_06-262.instructor: Zachary Ulissi (with Katie Whitehead, John Kitchin, Lynn Walker)
cmu_06-262.format: Jupyter notebook lecture notes; conda env via myenv.yml (not a Jupyter Book)

cmu_06-325.title: 06-325 Numerical Methods and ML for Chemical Engineering (Fall 2022)
cmu_06-325.format: Jupyter Book 1.x (f22-06-325/_config.yml + _toc.yml), Docker, pre-commit, GitHub Actions

ml_module: Bayesian optimization / active learning for design of experiments

cmu_06-325.relevance: CLOSEST MATCH to the target course: same title concept, same level, and the only reference with a developed ML module. Treat its ML sequence as the model for the AI half of this book.
cmu_06-325.caution: Repo is 817 MB; 373 MB is .git history and the rest is project datasets. Cloned shallow (--depth 1). Do not vendor its data directories.

ock_chme212.title: CHME 212 Scientific Computing (Spring 2026)
ock_chme212.level: undergraduate; assumes no programming beyond first-year ChemE

numerical_computation: ch11 linear algebra & matrices (+ matrix rank supplement)
planned_but_commented_out: ch19 image analysis for particle/phase characterization
ch21 simulation: Brownian motion / diffusion / random walks
structure.labs: lab01-lab11, paired to the chapter sequence

ock_chme212.relevance: The author's own prior course and the direct predecessor. Owns the numerical spine (ch10-18) and all lab infrastructure. Its README promises machine learning but no ML chapter exists yet - that gap is precisely what the new book fills.
ock_chme212.notes: 19 chapters + 11 labs already written. Reuse, don't rewrite. Chapters 00-09 are introductory programming and are likely below the junior/senior target level.
